key_insight: BT-QAOA approximates Max-k-Cut through binary MaxCut splits, reducing per-circuit quantum resources without directly encoding k assignments per vertex.
engineering_relevance: The approach could make multiway graph partitioning more practical on resource-limited quantum hardware by trading larger circuits for multiple smaller subproblem solves.
method: Run standard MaxCut QAOA on the full vertex set.
Repeatedly split the subset with the largest cut-value gain until the binary tree has k leaves.
Solve at most 2k−3 MaxCut subproblems, with a derived approximation bound tied to single-split quality.
evidence_signal: Numerical simulations report high approximation ratios, reduced per-circuit qubit and gate overhead, and orders-of-magnitude improvements in estimated single compiled-circuit success probability.
watch_item: Per-circuit savings do not establish lower total runtime, and the abstract reports simulations rather than hardware validation.
paper_title: Binary-Tree Quantum Approximate Optimization Algorithm for the Maximum $k$-Cut Problem
